title: Python CapabilityTable has the same LRU-eviction replay-floor hole as Rust had (fawm)
description: Mirror of the Rust fawm defect, found while fixing it: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/capability_announce.py CapabilityTable.record() LRU-evicts via self._entries.popitem(last=False) (:105) which drops the evicted announcer's seq entirely; cached_seq (:64-70) returns None for a missing entry, and the resource's verify call (:168) passes cached_seq=None -> the seq replay gate is skipped (if-not-None semantics in verify_capability_announcement). Identical attack to the filed Rust one: flood the table to evict a gateway, replay its older still-unexpired announcement, roll the table back. Fix (mirror the landed Rust fix): monotone per-IID seq-floor ledger captured at popitem eviction; cached_seq returns max(entry seq, floor); ledger bounded (drop lowest-iid stale floors when over capacity). Also note verify_capability_announcement's cached_seq=None path must keep refusing... check its semantics: if None means 'no gate', the fix MUST pass the floor from the ledger instead. Add tests mirroring capability.rs tests eviction_preserves_replay_floor and floor_ledger_stays_bounded. Note the restart-persistence gap applies to both stacks (table not persisted at all today) - durable floors tracked separately if wanted.
